questions.q: What does the @RestResource annotation do, and what must be true of the class it's applied to?
options: It exposes an Apex class as a custom REST endpoint; the class must be declared global
It exposes an Apex class as a SOAP web service; the class must be declared public
It schedules the class to run nightly; the class must implement Schedulable
It registers the class as an HttpCalloutMock; the class must be marked @isTest
questions.explain: @RestResource(urlMapping='/path/*') exposes a global Apex class as a custom REST endpoint reachable at /services/apexrest/path.

questions.q: How many times can the same HTTP-verb annotation (for example, @HttpGet) be used within a single Apex class?
options: As many times as needed, as long as each method has a different name
Exactly once per class
Up to four times, matching the four standard CRUD operations
Zero times — HTTP-verb annotations must go on the class, not a method
questions.explain: Each HTTP-verb annotation (@HttpGet, @HttpPost, @HttpPut, @HttpPatch, @HttpDelete) can be used only once per Apex class.

questions.q: What does RestContext.request give an Apex REST method access to?
options: Only the org's current governor limit usage
The incoming RestRequest, including requestURI, httpMethod, params, and requestBody
A list of all Named Credentials configured in the org
The WSDL for the current class
questions.explain: RestContext.request exposes the RestRequest object, which carries the details of the incoming HTTP request.

questions.q: What requirement applies to a method annotated with @HttpGet, @HttpPost, etc.?
options: It must be private and non-static
It must be global static
It must return a Database.SaveResult
It must be annotated with @future as well
questions.explain: Methods marked with the Apex REST HTTP-verb annotations must be declared global static.

questions.q: When does it make sense to build a custom Apex REST service instead of relying on Salesforce's standard REST API?
options: Never — the standard REST API always covers every use case
When the caller needs custom business logic, validation, or a response shape beyond plain record CRUD
Only when the caller uses SOAP instead of JSON
Only when Platform Events are also involved
questions.explain: The standard REST API already handles plain CRUD on any object with no code; Apex REST earns its place when custom logic, validation, or a different response shape is needed.
